line_sweep_scan.doc:
Read out monitored devices while a single device moves continuously from
start to stop. The readout is triggered by updates on the readback signal of the moving device
and may be throttled by setting a minimum update time. If a maximum update time is set, the readout
will be triggered if the time since the last update exceeds the maximum update time, even if no new update has been received.

Args:
    device (DeviceBase): device.
    start (float): start.
    stop (float): stop.
    relative (bool): Whether the positions are relative to the current position.
    exp_time (float [s]): Exposure time in seconds. Default: 0 s
    frames_per_trigger (int): Number of frames per trigger for devices that support configurable frame counts per trigger. Default: 1
    min_update (float [s]): min update. Default: 0 s
    max_update (float [s]): max update. Default: 0 s

Returns:
    ScanReport

Examples:
    Minimum:
        >>> scans.line_sweep_scan(dev.device, -1.0, 1.0, relative=False)
    Full:
        >>> scans.line_sweep_scan(dev.device, -1.0, 1.0, relative=False, exp_time=0, frames_per_trigger=1, min_update=0, max_update=0)

round_scan.doc:
A scan following a round shell-like pattern with increasing number of points in each ring. The scan starts at the inner ring and moves outwards.
The user defines the inner and outer radius, the number of rings and the number of positions in the first ring.

Exactly ``number_of_rings`` evenly spaced rings span the region outside
``inner_radius`` up to and including ``outer_radius``. A single ring lies
at ``outer_radius``. Ring ``k`` (starting at 1) contains
``k * pos_in_first_ring`` positions; no separate center point is generated.
For example, radii 0 and 2 with two rings and three positions in the first
ring produce nine positions at radii 1 and 2.

Args:
    motor_1 (DeviceBase): motor 1.
    motor_2 (DeviceBase): motor 2.
    inner_radius (float): inner radius.
    outer_radius (float): outer radius.
    number_of_rings (int): number of rings.
    pos_in_first_ring (int): pos in first ring.
    relative (bool): Whether the positions are relative to the current position.
    exp_time (float [s]): Exposure time in seconds. Default: 0 s
    frames_per_trigger (int): Number of frames per trigger for devices that support configurable frame counts per trigger. Default: 1
    settling_time (float [s]): Time to settle before trigger and readout. Default: 0 s
    settling_time_after_trigger (float [s]): Time to settle after the trigger but before the readout. Default: 0 s
    readout_time (float [s]): Configuration for devices that support configurable readout times. Default: 0 s
    center_1 (float): center 1. Default: 0
    center_2 (float): center 2. Default: 0
    burst_at_each_point (int): Number of triggers and readouts at each point. Default: 1

Returns:
    ScanReport

Examples:
    Minimum:
        >>> scans.round_scan(dev.motor_1, dev.motor_2, 1.0, 1.0, 1, 1, relative=False)
    Full:
        >>> scans.round_scan(dev.motor_1, dev.motor_2, 1.0, 1.0, 1, 1, relative=False, exp_time=0, frames_per_trigger=1, settling_time=0, settling_time_after_trigger=0, readout_time=0, center_1=0, center_2=0, burst_at_each_point=1)

Trigger and readout devices at a fixed interval.
Note that the interval time cannot be less than the exposure time.
The effective sleep time between points is:

    interval (float [s]): interval. s
    exp_time (float [s]): Exposure time in seconds. Default: 0 s
    settling_time (float [s]): Time to settle before trigger and readout. Default: 0 s

Returns:
    ScanReport

Examples:
    Minimum:
        >>> scans.time_scan(1, 1.0)
    Full:
        >>> scans.time_scan(1, 1.0, exp_time=0, settling_time=0)
